skill.name: doc-coauthoring
skill.description: Guide users through a structured workflow for co-authoring documentation, proposals, technical specs, decision docs, and RFCs.
skill.summary: Structured coauthoring workflow for drafting, refining, and reader-testing important documents.
skill.author: 7Spade

content.value_statement: Important documents often fail because key context stays in the author's head. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through context gathering, structured drafting, iterative refinement, and reader testing.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through context gathering before drafting begins.
Creates a section-by-section structure for documents, proposals, specs, and RFCs.
Supports brainstorming, curation, drafting, and focused edits for each section.
Prompts reader testing with a fresh Claude context to find gaps.
Encourages final checks for facts, links, audience fit, and desired impact.
limitations: Requires the user to provide accurate source context and review the final document.
Cannot access Slack, Teams, Drive, or SharePoint unless connectors are available and authorized.
Does not verify external facts, technical claims, or links without additional tools.
May take longer than freeform drafting because it emphasizes iteration and reader testing.

use_cases.title: Write a Technical Spec
use_cases.description: Turn rough architecture notes into a structured spec with clear trade-offs, risks, and open questions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Decision Document
use_cases.description: Create a decision record that explains context, options, rationale, consequences, and stakeholder concerns.

use_cases.title: Draft a Proposal
use_cases.description: Shape project context and goals into a proposal that readers can evaluate without private background knowledge.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Document
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a new document with guided context gathering.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me use the doc coauthoring workflow to write a [document type]. The audience is [audience], and the desired impact is [impact].

prompt_templates.title: Structure a Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert rough context into a document outline.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have shared the main context. Suggest a section structure for this [document type], explain why each section belongs, and ask what I want to adjust.

prompt_templates.title: Refine One Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a specific section through focused iteration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Work on the [section name] section. Ask clarifying questions, brainstorm possible points, help me choose what to keep, then draft the section.

prompt_templates.title: Run Reader Testing
prompt_templates.scenario: Check whether the document works for readers without prior context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Test this document like a fresh reader. Predict reader questions, identify ambiguity, list assumed knowledge, and recommend focused fixes.

output_examples.input: Draft a decision doc for adopting a new deployment model.
output_examples.output: A context interview, a decision-document outline, section drafts, targeted edit prompts, and reader-testing questions.

output_examples.input: Improve an existing technical spec before review.
output_examples.output: A gap analysis, section-level refinement steps, ambiguity checks, and a final review checklist for facts and audience fit.

output_examples.input: Write a proposal from scattered project notes.
output_examples.output: A structured proposal flow with goals, background, options, risks, stakeholder concerns, and next-step recommendations.

best_practices: Provide audience, document type, desired impact, and constraints before drafting.
Review each drafted section and give specific feedback about what to change.
Run reader testing before sharing the document with stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Starting with polished prose before enough context is gathered.
Skipping reader testing for documents that depend on hidden background knowledge.
Treating the generated document as final without checking facts, links, and technical details.

faq.question: What kinds of documents does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports documentation, proposals, technical specs, decision docs, RFCs, and similar structured writing tasks.

faq.question: Does it write the whole document at once?
faq.answer: No. It builds the document section by section so the user can refine content and style as work progresses.

faq.question: Can it use shared documents or team channels?
faq.answer: Only when authorized connectors or integrations are available. Otherwise, the user must paste the relevant context.

faq.question: What is reader testing?
faq.answer: Reader testing asks a fresh Claude context to answer likely reader questions and identify ambiguity or assumed knowledge.

faq.question: Is this useful for Codex or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide documentation work in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the workflow instructions are available.

faq.question: Who is responsible for the final document?
faq.answer: The user remains responsible for final quality, factual accuracy, links, technical details, and stakeholder fit.
